items.headline: Two trains collide in Egypt
items.summary: A collision between two trains in Egypt killed seven people and injured at least 125, PBS NewsHour reported. Rail accidents are common in Egypt, where the system has a history of mismanagement.

items.headline: Nebraska's Medicaid work rules hit snags
items.summary: Nebraska moved quickly to put Medicaid work requirements in place. Advocates say the rollout has had serious problems, including a cancer patient who was told he had lost coverage.

items.headline: Spain's housing crisis looms over snap election
items.summary: Spain faces a snap election called for Nov. 29 as a housing crisis grips the country. A TIME opinion piece examines the eviction and death of an elderly tenant.

digest.overview:
Congress returns Monday for a lame-duck session before Democrats take control of both chambers in January. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries backed an impeachment resolution against Pete Hegseth led by outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie, as Democrats ready investigations that Trump and his Justice Department are resisting. Stephen Miller starts Monday as White House chief of staff, and Trump said he was kidding about offering Dana White the press secretary job. The Supreme Court is weighing a case that could shield federal officers from lawsuits as complaints about ICE agents rise. Nvidia's board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang over alleged ties to a Chinese spy.

Abroad, Trump said the U.S. land blockade of Iran is in effect and that renewed strikes are "highly unlikely" if talks on Tehran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz progress. Israel's President Isaac Herzog formally gave Gadi Eisenkot six weeks to form a government; his alliance holds 48 seats to 53 for Netanyahu's bloc, short of the 61 needed. The Kremlin said it hopes the U.S. midterm shake-up won't change Trump's push for a Ukraine deal. Poland began two days of mourning after the Krakow shooting, and police found the attacker's parents and sister dead at his home. Two trains collided in Egypt, killing at least seven. Okinawa's governor will seek a review of the U.S.-Japan troops agreement after an alleged murder by a U.S. Marine. Pope Leo arrived in Argentina, and COP31 climate talks opened in Antalya, Turkey, amid frustration over the limited focus on fossil fuels.

home.overview:
The Bears edged the Buccaneers 27–24 on Sunday night to reach 7-2, the Packers piled up 45 points against the Patriots, and the Bengals beat the Falcons 34–17 in Madrid. The Saints outlasted Shedeur Sanders' Browns 23–22 in overtime, the 49ers improved to 7-1 by beating the Raiders 38–17, and the Broncos won at Carolina to go 7-2. Patrick Mahomes' MRI showed no significant elbow damage, and the Colts say Daniel Jones won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline. Bills at Vikings, both 6-1, closes Week 9 tonight. In the NBA, Philadelphia beat Chicago 127–121 to join the Lakers at 9-2, Cooper Flagg led Dallas past Brooklyn 130–93, and Boston won 117–97 in Milwaukee; eight games are on tonight.

Barcelona won 2–1 at Atlético to move three points clear of Real Madrid in La Liga. Liverpool won 3–1 at Crystal Palace, Brighton climbed to second by beating Brentford, Sunderland stunned Chelsea 1–0, and Man United and Aston Villa drew 4–4. Freiburg rose to third in the Bundesliga, and Lille won at Rennes to sit two points behind PSG in Ligue 1. Non-league Wimborne Town knocked Crawley out of the FA Cup. The international break starts now, with England hosting Croatia and Italy facing France in the Nations League on Thursday.

brief: Samsung beat KT Wiz 12–1 in Game 5 in Daegu to win the Korean Series 4–1, their first title since 2014 and ninth overall.
An eight-run fifth inning, helped by a KT error, decided the clincher, with Won Tae-in allowing one run over five innings.
Captain Koo Ja-wook was named series MVP after hitting .500 (10-for-20) with a home run and six RBIs.
Samsung lost Game 1 in Suwon before winning four straight, and 41-year-old catcher Kang Min-ho won his first title.

Five retired umpires, including Joe West, sued alleging they are owed more than $2 million in miscalculated benefits.
